How to Use This Database

This is a single self-contained file. No account, no install, and once you have a copy, no internet connection required.

Use it here

Search, filter and sort from the bar above. Click any Direction, Issues, Notes or Review cell to change it — useful if you disagree with a call, or want to mark up the bills that matter to your state. Click a bill number to open its full text. Use States for a written overview of any jurisdiction and a sortable table of every state, and Trends for charts that redraw as you change the filters. Year, State and Issue let you tick more than one; with several issues ticked you see bills carrying any of them.

Or keep your own copy

Press Cmd+S (Mac) or Ctrl+S (Windows) and choose “Webpage, HTML Only.” You get one file you can open any time by double-clicking it, keep in a shared drive, or mark up without touching anyone else’s version. A saved copy falls back to a standard system typeface, so it will look slightly different from this page.

Your edits are yours alone

Changes are saved in whichever browser you are using. They never reach me, and they are not visible to anyone else. That also means they do not travel: edits made on this page will not appear in a copy you download, and edits in your downloaded copy will not appear here. Each copy keeps its own notes.

Updates keep your edits — a backup keeps them safe

When this page is updated, your edits carry over automatically as long as you come back in the same browser on the same device: they are saved in that browser and re-applied to each new version, and a banner tells you when that has happened. A change you made to a bill stays in place even if the published version of that bill changes later. If a bill is removed from the database, or its number or year is corrected, your edit to it stays in your backup file but no longer shows on the page. Edits do not survive clearing your browser data, switching browser or device, or moving between this page and a downloaded copy, and some browsers clear saved data on their own: Safari, and every browser on an iPhone or iPad, may delete it if you have not visited the page for about a week. The Edits button saves everything you have changed as a .json file: use it as a backup, to move your work to another computer, to hand it to a colleague, or to send it to me so corrections can be baked into the master copy. The Edits window shows when you last saved a backup.

Tell me what is wrong with it

If you find errors, bills I have missed, or classifications you disagree with, please use the Submit Feedback form at the top of the page. It goes straight into the review queue, which is faster than email and means nothing gets lost. That is the main reason this is public.

About This Database

What this is. Juvenile Justice Legislation In The US is a searchable record of the juvenile justice bills signed into law in all 50 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico from 2021 through 2026. It starts from the enacted bills tracked by the National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL), plus a small number added by hand where NCSL missed them. For each bill you get the state, bill number, title, a plain summary, sponsors and cosponsors, enactment date and a link to the bill itself. On top of that, every bill has been read and coded by hand: whether it moves youth justice toward reform or toward more punitive treatment (or is mixed, or administrative), which issues it touches (from transfer to adult court and detention conditions to fines and fees, truancy and records), and notes where something needs flagging. The States view adds a written overview of each jurisdiction's record.

Why it matters. Juvenile justice law changes state by state, often with little coverage, so it is hard to see what has actually been enacted or which way it is moving. This puts six years of enacted law in one place, read and classified consistently, so advocates, funders and policy staff can compare states and track issues without starting from scratch.

This database was built by Ad Astra Consulting, LLC to support juvenile justice advocacy, coalition partners, and policy research.

Source data. Bill information (state, bill number, title, summary, sponsor, enactment date, and topic tags) is drawn from the National Conference of State Legislatures (NCSL) Juvenile Justice Legislation Database, accessed via annual data pulls. NCSL is not affiliated with this database, has not reviewed it, and does not endorse its analysis or characterizations.

Scope note — Child Welfare*. This database covers juvenile justice legislation as captured by the NCSL Juvenile Justice Legislation Database. Bills carrying the Child Welfare* tag are juvenile justice bills that also appear in NCSL's separate Child Welfare Enacted Legislation Database, generally because they touch dependency court process. The Child Welfare database itself is not incorporated in this build.

Scope note — 2026 is partial. Coverage runs 2021–2026. 2026 may be incomplete, so totals, reform-to-punitive ratios, and trend lines that include 2026 are provisional. Scope is enacted bills only, which hides states where reform legislation passed one chamber and stalled.

Analytical layer. The Direction labels (Reform / Punitive / Administrative / Mixed), Issue tags, Flag designations, and Notes are the work of Ad Astra Consulting and reflect editorial judgment. An initial pass used a keyword heuristic, which proved unreliable and is not relied on here: all six years (2021–2026) have since been hand-reviewed, and the Direction labels and Issue tags in this build reflect that review rather than automated output. Flagged rows mark specific open questions — a thin NCSL summary, an ambiguous provision, or a classification still under discussion — not unreviewed bills.

Use & redistribution. This database is built for advocacy, research, and educational use, but it is not restricted to those uses: the license below permits any use, including commercial use. The one condition is attribution — please cite both Ad Astra Consulting, LLC and the underlying NCSL source when redistributing or quoting.
